title: Practice 4: с-: down, and together — раз-: apart

blocks.text: Exercises: sentences from Tatoeba (tatoeba.org, CC BY 2.0 FR) and from the library's public-domain books.

exercises.q: Зрители с криком ___ (разбежаться / разбегаться).
exercises.why: The prefix "с-" implies the following meanings: (a) to descend, to go down: Мы съезжаем с горы. — DLI, Lesson 63.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.prompt: With a scream, the spectators scattered.
exercises.context: The prefix "с-" implies the following meanings: (a) to descend, to go down: Мы съезжаем с горы.

exercises.q: The upstart tried to pass for a man of culture.
exercises.why: The prefix "с-" implies the following meanings: (a) to descend, to go down: Мы съезжаем с горы. Он сходит вниз по лестнице. (b) to come off, to drive off: Автомобиль съехал с дороги. Поезд сошёл с пути. Note that these verbs (сходить, съезжать, etc.) are usually followed by the preposition с + Gen. Wiktionary's two entries for «сходить»: сходи́ть • (sxodítʹ) impf (perfective сойти́) — to go down, to come down, to descend, to get off; to come off, to disappear; сходи́ть • (sxodítʹ) impf (perfective сойти́) — to go down, to come down, to descend, to get off; to come off, to disappear. — DLI, Lesson 63.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: The prefix "с-" implies the following meanings: (a) to descend, to go down: Мы съезжаем с горы. (DLI, Lesson 63)

exercises.q: Очки постоянно ___ (сползать / сползти) мне на нос.
exercises.why: The imperfective aspect emphasizes the action itself. — From the DLI Grammar Reference Book, Lesson 37.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.prompt: My glasses keep slipping down my nose.
exercises.context: The imperfective aspect emphasizes the action itself.

exercises.q: ___ (свести / сводить), пожалуйста, мат к минимуму.
exercises.why: **свести́** — **своди́ть** — to lead, to take (from somewhere); to bring together, to throw together. **свезти́** — **свози́ть** — (perfective only, transitive) to transport, to drive, to convey; (colloquial, perfective only, transitive) to transport there and back, to drive there and back. **сле́зть** — **слеза́ть** — to come down, to get down (from), to dismount (from); (colloquial) to come down. **сойти́сь** — **сходи́ться** — to meet, to come together; to converge, to coalesce. — DLI, Lesson 63.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.prompt: Please keep the swearing to a minimum.
exercises.context: свести́** — **своди́ть — to lead, to take (from somewhere); to bring together, to throw together.

exercises.q: Господин Горбачёв, ___ (снести / сносить) эту стену!
exercises.why: **снести́** — **сноси́ть** — to carry down; to carry to. **свести́** — **своди́ть** — to lead, to take (from somewhere); to bring together, to throw together. **свезти́** — **свози́ть** — (perfective only, transitive) to transport, to drive, to convey; (colloquial, perfective only, transitive) to transport there and back, to drive there and back. **сле́зть** — **слеза́ть** — to come down, to get down (from), to dismount (from); (colloquial) to come down. — DLI, Lesson 63.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.prompt: Mr Gorbachev, tear down this wall!
exercises.context: снести́** — **сноси́ть — to carry down; to carry to.

exercises.q: Том ___ (свозить / свезти) свою собаку к ветеринару.
exercises.why: **свезти́** — **свози́ть** — (perfective only, transitive) to transport, to drive, to convey; (colloquial, perfective only, transitive) to transport there and back, to drive there and back. **сле́зть** — **слеза́ть** — to come down, to get down (from), to dismount (from); (colloquial) to come down. **сойти́сь** — **сходи́ться** — to meet, to come together; to converge, to coalesce. **съе́хаться** — **съезжа́ться** — to meet (on one's way); to assemble, to come together, to gather. — DLI, Lesson 63.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.prompt: Tom took his dog to the vet.
exercises.context: свезти́** — **свози́ть — (perfective only, transitive) to transport, to drive, to convey; (colloquial, perfective only, transitive) to transport there and back, to drive there and back.

exercises.q: Она хотела ___ (сбежать / сбегать) от повседневности.
exercises.why: Дети сбежались на детскую площадь. — The children ran (from all directions) to the playground. — в / на + acc.; к + dat.. **раз-, разо-, рас- (+сь, +ся)** — Divergent movement in various directions from one center. — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_grammar#Verbs_of_motion, CC BY-SA 4.0)  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.prompt: She wanted to get away from everyday life.
exercises.context: Дети сбежались на детскую площадь. — The children ran (from all directions) to the playground. — в / на + acc.; к + dat..

exercises.q: Птицы ___ (разлететься / разлетаться) в разные стороны.
exercises.why: **разлете́ться** — **разлета́ться** — to fly away, to scatter (in the air); to come apart, to be blown apart. **разбежа́ться** — **разбега́ться** — to scatter; to take a run, to run up (before jumping, diving, etc). **разнести́** — **разноси́ть** — to carry, to convey, to deliver; (colloquial) (news, rumor etc) to spread around. **развести́** — **разводи́ть** — to take along, to bring; to conduct; to part, to move apart, to pull apart, to separate. — DLI, Lesson 63.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.prompt: The birds flew away in all directions.
exercises.context: разлете́ться** — **разлета́ться — to fly away, to scatter (in the air); to come apart, to be blown apart.

exercises.q: Здесь ___ (разносить / разнести) почту два раза в день.
exercises.why: **разнести́** — **разноси́ть** — to carry, to convey, to deliver; (colloquial) (news, rumor etc) to spread around. **развести́** — **разводи́ть** — to take along, to bring; to conduct; to part, to move apart, to pull apart, to separate. **развезти́** — **развози́ть** — to deliver, to transport (multiple people or things to their respective destinations); (colloquial, impersonal). — DLI, Lesson 63.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.prompt: Mail delivery here is twice a day.
exercises.context: разнести́** — **разноси́ть — to carry, to convey, to deliver; (colloquial) (news, rumor etc) to spread around.
